lesson_title: Macro Practice Run: How Marks Are Won, Question by Question
hook_text: Every mark in Economics is won the same way. Here's the machine — question by question.
clip_script: A full macro practice run, and one habit decides everything: match your effort to the marks. Two marks, one word: money entering the circular flow through investment, government spending and exports — injections. Banked. Short answers: name TWO instruments of fiscal policy — taxation, government spending. One line each, never a paragraph. Then the data. Can you read this business cycle? Crest: peak. Falling section: recession. Bottom: trough — and the distance between two crests is the LENGTH of the cycle, the number forecasters live by. Calculations are number sentences: receipts one thousand five hundred, payments one thousand six hundred and fifty, transfers plus thirty — current account minus one hundred and twenty million. Setup line, totals, labelled answer: every step is a mark. And the essay is four boxes: define for 2, develop for 20, judge for 6, land one fresh thought for 2. Nothing here asks for genius. It asks for pieces, delivered in order — and after this run, you know every piece by name.
visual_style: A stack of practice questions dealing out like cards, each stamped with its mark value; a wave diagram labelling peak, recession, trough and cycle length; number sentences coupling together like train carriages; the essay as four boxes filling 2, 20, 6, 2.
pacing: Quick hits through the recall items, a measured beat on the data reading, a strong four-count rhythm on the essay boxes.
call_to_action: Do the full practice run and walk into your final exams already knowing how every mark is won.
